title: Disputing Lester's story of switching to tenor; his father took his horns
summary: Phillips rejects Lester's tape story that he asked for a tenor, saying Lester played tenor throughout with Bronson, and that his father kept all his instruments.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well, the story I heard on the tape that Lester made, he said there was a tenor player in Bronson's band, and nobody liked him. So he went with Bronson one day and said, "Fire that guy and get me a tenor."
Ain't nothin' like that, man. That's phony.
Well, that's what Lester said on a tape.
Lester said that himself?
Yeah. He said nobody in the band liked this guy, and finally Bronson just... Lester went up to Bronson and said, "I'm playing alto, but give me a tenor."
I don't see how he could say that. Lester never did play no alto with Bronson.
He never did play alto with Bronson.
He played tenor the whole time.
So in other words, he switched to tenor when he got in Bronson's because that's what Bronson wanted? He was playing alto right before Bronson, right?

He was playing alto with his father's band. So he left his father's band and went with Bronson. Any time he left his father, his father was taking everything he had. He took all the horns... Let's see, what did he have? He had a clarinet, a baritone and an alto -- those were the instruments -- and a soprano.
Clarinet, baritone, alto and soprano. That's what Lester
Phillips - 81
was playing.
Yeah, that's his instruments. You'd see them standing on that stand...
So he took all those away from him.
He took his clothes, too. He left everything. The only clothes Les had is what he had on.
Oh, he left his stuff. Lester Young didn't take...
No, he just left it.
He just left it. I see.
Yeah.
